title: Ballads, waltzes and the old jazz repertoire on record
summary: He loved jazz first but also ballads and waltzes, and recalls two-bit club tunes and records of the Halfway House and NORK.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: What else do they play? Do they play waltzes or anything on your own?

Oh yeah, yeah, yeah. I always go back and remember the pretty tunes, you know. I always loved ballads and pretty waltzes as well as these jazz tunes, you see. I just get a lot of kick out of playing all of them. I love the jazz first, but I also like to play ballads and pretty waltzes. In those days, I think the emphasis was on that. I mean, they knew a lot about pretty music, and they knew how to play it, too. Of course, these bands, like in these two-bits clubs they used to have around here, those fellas could really play that jazz, clarinet, marmalade, and baratarian, oh man. All those old tunes, those fine old tunes. We had them all on record, and somehow through the years they slipped away. Like the Halfway House Band, I think they made a lot of fine records, and... I don't know, in those days there's so many good ones. New Orleans Rhythm, Kings, and I should have more of their records, but I do not have one.
Do you remember hearing the Brunus Brothers around here?
I remember hearing them on the records, but I was too small to go into clubs then, you see.
